clue.text: Masculine, yet extremely childish

parts.note: yet as a conjunction means but

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters, of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone is described as manly but also very babyish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'childish' but takes that word's first and last letters, C and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Butch is an informal adjective for a tough, conspicuously manly look or manner.

clue.text: Money for section of the orchestra

definitions.meaning: the group of metal wind instruments

explanation.surface: Cash is needed for the trumpets and trombones.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is British slang for cash, and also the orchestral family of trumpets, horns and trombones.

clue.text: One harasses people in the hills

indicators.note: in places the word for people within the pair of hills

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor; two of them stand for the plural hills
people means men

explanation.surface: Someone bothers the folk who live up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a craggy hill typical of Dartmoor in south-west England; the plural 'hills' is met by a pair of them around the people.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is a person who persecutes or harasses others.

clue.text: Committed socialists had quit without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so had wraps round the letter for resistance

parts.note: taken as written
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance
quit in the past tense means left

explanation.surface: Dedicated socialists walked out without putting up a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking' but here means 'outside', so HAD goes around R.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard left is the uncompromising, radical wing of socialist politics.

clue.text: Learner I told off is not kept in detention

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British car
told off means scolded, berated

explanation.surface: A pupil scolded by a teacher is let out rather than kept after school.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone freed from captivity, no longer held, has been set free.

clue.text: Song is appreciated without middle part

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter synonym is dropped

parts.note: appreciated means liked

explanation.surface: A tune is enjoyed apart from its central section.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is a German art song, as by Schubert.

clue.text: Where soldiers have morning dips?

parts.note: soldiers are not troops but strips of toast, dunked at breakfast into soft yolks

explanation.surface: It sounds like troops taking an early swim.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are thin fingers of buttered toast dipped into a soft yolk at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast fingers are dipped into soft-cooked eggs in their shells at breakfast.

clue.text: Transported yellow bird

parts.note: transported in the sense of enraptured means rapt
or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A yellow bird has been carried somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A raptor is a bird of prey such as a hawk or eagle.

clue.text: A number getting hot in plane, perhaps

indicators.note: in puts the letter for hot inside the tree

parts.note: the plane is a kind of tree, so this is a definition by example
H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone's temperature climbs on board an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a cardinal number, one more than two.

clue.text: Nonconformist affected tiredness

indicators.note: affected in the sense of altered or disturbed signals a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A rebel puts on a show of being weary.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter, historically, is a Protestant who refused to conform to the Church of England.

clue.text: Following Great North Road, rider is lost in Scottish town

indicators.note: following means the next piece comes after the road's letters

parts.note: the A1 road, written AI in crosswords, was called the Great North Road

indicators.note: lost suggests the word rider has gone astray and is jumbled

explanation.surface: A cyclist goes up the old main road to the north and loses the way in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 ran from London to Edinburgh as the Great North Road; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Airdrie is a town in North Lanarkshire, east of Glasgow.

clue.text: Teaches naughty child tricks

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
arts in the sense of wiles or tricks

explanation.surface: A mischievous child shows others how to play pranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart knowledge is to pass it on, which is what a teacher does.

clue.text: Former Liberal leader backed by English writer

indicators.note: backed by means followed by, the next letter coming after

parts.note: David Steel led the British Liberal Party from 1976 to 1988

explanation.surface: An ex-party leader gets support from an English author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English writer' wants to be the definition, but E is needed in the wordplay; Richard Steele was an Irish-born essayist, co-founder of The Spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Steele was an essayist and playwright of the early eighteenth century.

clue.text: Italian individual captivated by poetry

indicators.note: captivated by means held inside the word for poetry

parts.note: poetry means verse
an individual is one

explanation.surface: Someone is spellbound by poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Paolo Veronese was a Venetian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Clergyman suffering under pressure, it's generally accepted

indicators.note: in a down clue under means the clergyman and illness sit below the letter for pressure

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman's title
suffering means ailing

explanation.surface: A vicar is unwell from stress, as everyone agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A prevailing view is the one most widely held, current and dominant.

clue.text: Not working, like former monk

definitions.meaning: a monk who has left his religious order

explanation.surface: A broken machine is compared to an ex-monk.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken machines bear this phrase, and a monk who has quit his religious order is literally outside it.

clue.text: Expenses incurred abroad, travelling south

parts.note: abroad in the sense of out and about means out
travelling means going
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Costs mount while on a trip overseas heading south.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings is the British term for money spent, expenditure.

clue.text: Notice son is hooked on drug

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A parent realises a son is addicted to drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see or notice it.

clue.text: Poor writer on Egyptian river boat

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the Nile flows through Egypt
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An impoverished author is aboard a vessel on the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: Penniless means having no money at all, destitute.

clue.text: Town supplying books penned by Greene?

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, the books placed inside the first name

parts.note: Graham Greene was the novelist, so his first name is suggested
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A place provides novels written by Graham Greene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like 'written' but means 'enclosed'. Grantham is a Lincolnshire market town, birthplace of Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Grantham is a market town in Lincolnshire, England.

clue.text: Heard bird go off

indicators.note: heard signals that the bird's name is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone hears a bird fly away.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk that goes off, spoiling, is said to turn sour.

clue.text: US actress curiously arranged tours round Virginia

indicators.note: tours round means the jumbled letters go around the state's abbreviation
curiously signals the letters of arranged are put in an odd order

parts.note: VA is the US postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: An American film star oddly organises tours round a southern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' makes AGARDNER from the fodder, and 'tours round' means those letters encircle the state's abbreviation, which lands after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ava Gardner was a Hollywood film star of the 1940s and 1950s.

clue.text: React with disgust concerning form of contraception

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a coil is an intrauterine contraceptive device

explanation.surface: Someone is repelled by a method of birth control.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to flinch or draw back in horror or distaste.

clue.text: Anti-hero in play being broadcast

indicators.note: in play suggests the letters of anti-hero are moved about freely

explanation.surface: A flawed protagonist appears in a drama on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme going out live on radio or television is said to be transmitting.

clue.text: Bound to have king arrested and dealt with in court

indicators.note: arrested means held, so the king's letter is caught inside

parts.note: bound means tied
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is detained, tied up and put on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A case or a defendant that has been tried has been heard and judged by a court.

clue.text: One in seven surprisingly breaks last commandment

indicators.note: in places the numeral within the jumbled seven
surprisingly signals that the letters of seven come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One of seven people unexpectedly breaks the final commandment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tenth Commandment forbids coveting a neighbour's goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth commandment forbids coveting, so one who covets another's goods breaks it.

clue.text: Strict schoolmaster? Not a bit of it

indicators.note: a bit of it means a small portion of the preceding words is taken out

explanation.surface: Is a schoolmaster strict? Not at all, comes the reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a bit of it' reads as a denial, but 'a bit of it' marks letters lifted from 'schoolmaster? Not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means severe and uncompromising, as with a strict teacher.

clue.text: Quick way to diet

definitions.meaning: going without food for a time

explanation.surface: A speedy way to lose weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means rapid, and also to abstain from food, a common method of dieting.

clue.text: Distinguished chap keeps cool, beginning to increase capital

indicators.note: keeps in the sense of holds or retains means the posh chap's word wraps round the word for cool

parts.note: a nob is a person of high social standing
to air something is to cool or ventilate it

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A wealthy man saves money to start building up funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Sportsman allowed in to swim topless

indicators.note: in places the word for allowed inside
topless removes the top, the first letter, of the word for swim

parts.note: to bathe is to swim
allowed means let

explanation.surface: A sportsman is permitted to go swimming without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter of the swimming verb, leaving ATHE, and 'in' puts the word for allowed inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person who competes in sports, especially track and field.

clue.text: Car accessory needed: small one, please

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
I is the Roman numeral one
to please is to delight

explanation.surface: A motorist asks for a small one of something for the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a small lamp at the front of a vehicle.

clue.text: Mother's working as homemaker?

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, with the possessive s
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Mum is busy keeping house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homemaker' suggests a housewife, but a stonemason literally builds homes; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason constructs buildings, so is literally a builder of houses.
